ego-splitting can be used to find the best partition of a graph in terms of a given objective function, and the solution of this optimization problem is the optimal partitioning of the ego-nets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local structures of ego-nets, which are known to be highly predictive for the global structure of the network, are also predictive for the local structures of overlapping clusters.
ego-nets are an important tool for understanding complex networks, and that they can be leveraged to develop scalable, flexible and theoretically sound community detection methods.
